owns.rule: Beta 1.0 uses one authoritative local Python host process per canonical data instance and a browser client on the same machine.
The host process, not the browser window, owns application lifetime and background-work continuity.
Authoritative operation is exposed only through a supported exact loopback origin. Remote-listen modes are outside Beta 1.0.
Beta source, persistence, migrations, packaging, and release lineage remain independent from Alpha/Zeus.
The HLD preserves the accepted Windows 10/11 x64 and Python 3.13/3.14 support matrix and forbids an installed Node.js runtime dependency.
The product and release artifacts remain proprietary/internal and runtime/customer material is excluded from source control.

does_not_own.capability: database schema, migrations, connection policy, and durable job persistence
browser interaction semantics and frontend implementation
cryptographic choices, local-run trust protocol details, diagnostics security, backup/recovery
transaction, audit, temporal, history, idempotency, and derived-state semantics
exact Python server framework and loopback-port mechanics
exact frontend framework, client language and browser build tooling
exact tray toolkit, installer technology and supported-browser/package integration

authority_rules: Browser code may request commands and queries but may not establish domain validity by itself.
Adapters and background jobs may discover or stage evidence but may not bypass application-service/domain mutation policies.
No module may mutate another module's authoritative persistence through undocumented table/file shortcuts.
Cross-domain behavior must use explicit application/service interfaces or reproducible projections.
A technical convenience process, cache, registry, or file never becomes independent product/domain authority.
